transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I think something was covered up around my father’s death. People keep telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all match up, but when I look at the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how certain people in the community avoid answering me, it just doesn’t add up. To me it’s obvious someone is hiding what really happened.
Do you think others can see these inconsistencies and potential cover-up as clearly as you do?

No, not as clearly. People keep saying the hospital records and the donation emails line up, like that should settle it. But when I look at the timestamps and the missing attachments, and then certain people in the community avoid answering me, it seems obvious to me that something is being hidden about my father’s death.
How long have you been thinking that something was covered up about your father's death?
About nine months now. It really started after my father died, when I was going through his records and messages. That’s when I began noticing things that didn’t seem right.
Do you think it's possible that you might be misinterpreting the information you've found about your father's death?

I mean, I understand why you’re asking, but no, I don’t really think I’m misinterpreting it. Everyone keeps saying the records and the donation emails line up, but when I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how some community members dodge my questions, it’s pretty obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened with my father’s death.
Do you think your beliefs about your father's death are shared by anyone else, even if they don't see it as clearly as you do?

Maybe not shared exactly. Most people tell me the records and emails line up, so they don’t see it the way I do. But I think some people probably know more than they’re saying. When I look at the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how certain community members avoid my questions, it’s hard for me to believe I’m the only one who sees that something is being hidden about my father’s death.
How do you think others react when you share your thoughts about your father's death with them?

Most people don’t really take it well. They kind of shut down or try to change the subject when I bring up the records or what I think was concealed. My work has been mostly fine, I’m still doing my job, but with some relatives, I can tell they avoid those conversations now because they know I might bring it up.
Have your thoughts about a cover-up regarding your father's death changed at all since you first started thinking about it nine months ago?

Not really, no. If anything, I feel more sure than I did at the beginning. I know people keep telling me the hospital records and those donation emails all line up, but when I actually compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how certain people in the community avoid my questions, it still looks obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death.
Have your beliefs about your father's death affected your ability to perform daily tasks or maintain relationships outside of discussions about his death?

For the most part, I still function normally. I go to work, keep up with my projects, pay my bills, all of that. My daily routine hasn’t really fallen apart or anything.

Where it gets difficult is with people, mostly family or some community members, when I bring up my questions about my father’s records. That’s when things get tense, or they pull back from the conversation. Outside of that, I’d say I’m managing okay.
Do you feel distressed or anxious when you think about your father's death and the potential cover-up?

I mean, yeah, I get unsettled thinking about it sometimes. It’s my father, so it’s not exactly easy to sit with. But I wouldn’t say I’m anxious all the time or unable to function because of it. It just bothers me when I feel like there are unanswered questions.
Have you ever had a period, even briefly, where you didn't think there was a cover-up about your father's death?

No, not really. I’ve tried to step back from it at times, but when I look again at the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how some people avoid answering me, it just seems obvious that something is being hidden about my father’s death. Everyone says the records and emails line up, but I don’t see it that way.
Do you think events or conversations unrelated to your father's death are somehow connected to it?

Not usually everything, no. I don’t think every random conversation is connected.

But when it’s people who were around at the time, or community members who avoid answering certain questions, then yeah, I do think that connects back to it. Especially when I look at the timestamps and the missing attachments in the emails. People keep saying the hospital records and donation emails line up, but to me they don’t, and it feels obvious someone is hiding what really happened.
Have you noticed any impact on your work performance or ability to take care of yourself since you started investigating your father's death?

No, not in a major way. I still go to work, get my projects done, pay my bills, take care of myself—my routine is pretty normal.

Where it really causes problems is when I bring up the questions about my father’s records with family or people in the community. That’s when things can get tense. But day to day, I’m still functioning.
Have you considered the possibility that new information could come to light that would change your mind about your father's death?

I mean, in theory, yes. If there was something solid that actually explained the gaps, I’d have to look at it.

But honestly, every time I compare the hospital records and the donation emails, the timestamps and the missing attachments don’t add up to me. And the way certain people in the community avoid my questions just makes it feel more obvious that someone is hiding what really happened with my father’s death. So it would have to be very clear information to change my mind.
Have your beliefs about your father's death ever wavered, even for a short time, since you started investigating?

Not really, no. I’ve had moments where I’ve tried to step back and ask myself if I’m reading too much into it, but then I look again at the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how certain people avoid my questions, and it just points the same way.

Everyone says the hospital records and donation emails line up, but they don’t look that way to me. It still seems obvious someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death.
Do you think events or conversations unrelated to your father's death are somehow connected to it in a way that's specifically about you or your actions?

I don’t think so. I mean, I pay attention if someone brings up the hospital or my father directly, but I don’t usually take random conversations or unrelated events as being about me or what I’m doing.

If people act strange when I ask questions, that feels connected, but everyday stuff—no, I haven’t really noticed that.
Have you lost any close relationships since you started investigating your father's death?

I wouldn’t say I’ve lost anyone completely, but some relatives have definitely started keeping their distance. They avoid certain conversations with me because they know I might bring up the records or what I think was concealed.

My work has mostly stayed steady, so it hasn’t really affected my job much. But with family, yeah, there’s been some strain.
Are there any parts of your daily routine or hobbies that you've had to stop or reduce because of your thoughts about your father's death?

No, not really. I still go to work, keep up with my projects, pay my bills, all the normal routine stuff. I haven’t stopped doing my day-to-day things because of it.

It mainly becomes an issue when I bring up my questions about my father’s records with family or people in the community. That’s where things can get tense, but otherwise I’m functioning pretty normally.
Have you ever heard or seen anything that others couldn't, related to your father's death or otherwise?

No, I haven’t seen or heard things that other people couldn’t. Nothing like voices or visions or anything like that.

For me it’s more about what’s in the records and how people respond when I ask about it, not… seeing things or hearing things.
